title: Starting up a project: activities, inputs, outputs and RACI
blurb: Apply the eight starting up activities to a scenario and say who is accountable, responsible and consulted for the appointments and the outline business case.
question: The executive asks the project manager to choose and appoint the senior user. Is this an appropriate application of the 'appoint the project management team' activity, and why?

teach.h: From naming activities to applying them
teach.body: Formally: starting up a project makes sure the prerequisites for initiating are in place, through eight activities with recommended actions and a RACI table (13.4, 13.6). In plain English: at Practitioner level you are shown someone doing something before initiation and asked which activity it is, whether it was done the way the manual recommends, and whether the right role did it.

teach.body: Responsible means the role that does the work; accountable means the role that owns the result and signs it off; consulted means asked before the decision; informed means told afterwards. 'Not involved' is a real answer too. In starting up, the business layer owns the appointments, the executive makes them, and the project manager is not involved in appointing the team.

teach.h: Answering 'is this appropriate?' for a starting up activity
items: Name the activity from what is being done, not from the words in the stem.
Recall its recommended action (for example consult the executive, senior user and senior supplier for the PPD).
Check the role: is the person doing it the one the RACI expects?
Pick the reason that explains THIS situation; a true statement about another activity is a distractor.

teach.body: Fernhollow's board makes managing director Imogen Fairley executive, and she appoints Nadia Osei as project manager. Nadia asks the technical manager about past product launches and opens a lessons log. She runs a workshop with Imogen and the senior user and supplier to agree the outline business case and the PPD. Imogen appoints the rest of the team. The approach is hybrid, with two recipes co-manufactured. Nadia assembles the brief, plans a four-week initiation and requests initiation.

rows.label: Outline business case
values: High-level; PPD agreed with board roles
Detailed costs before a plan exists

rows.label: Assess previous lessons
values: Ask people who ran similar projects
Skip it because the team is new

rows.label: Request initiation
values: Verbal pitch with no initiation plan

teach.text: Classic traps: the project manager is NOT involved in appointing the project management team (business layer accountable, executive responsible). The initiation stage plan is made in starting up, not in managing a stage boundary. 'Authorize initiation' is the board's response in directing a project, not a starting up activity.

items: Eight activities, triggered by the mandate, ending with request project initiation.
Appointments: business layer accountable, executive responsible; PM not involved in appointing the team.
Outline business case: PM consults executive, senior user and senior supplier and creates the PPD.
Starting up is not complete until the initiation stage plan exists.

summary: You can now recognize each starting up activity in a scenario, name its inputs and outputs, and judge whether it was carried out as the manual recommends. You can also apply the starting up RACI cells for the appointments and the consultation behind the outline business case.

A.q: Fernhollow Foods is starting up its Fernhollow Kitchen launch. The project manager asks the technical manager, who ran two earlier product launches, what went wrong on them and records the points before any planning starts. Which activity is being carried out, and why is it appropriate?
options: Assess previous lessons, because it draws on people with experience of similar projects
Prepare the outline business case, because past launches show which benefits to expect
Select the project approach, because earlier launches show how the work should be done
Appoint the project management team, because the manager could become project assurance
A.why: Assess previous lessons creates the lessons log by consulting individuals or teams with experience of similar projects (13.4.2).

whyNot.1: The outline business case sets out the high-level justification; asking what went wrong on earlier launches is lesson gathering.
whyNot.2: Lessons can inform the approach, but asking about past problems and recording them is the lessons activity.
whyNot.3: Nothing is being appointed; the action is gathering lessons.

A.q: At Fernhollow Foods, the board of directors acts as the business layer for the Fernhollow Kitchen project. It has decided who will be executive, and the executive will then appoint a project manager. Which role should be accountable for the 'appoint the executive and the project manager' activity?
options: The executive
The project manager
The business layer
Project assurance
A.why: In tab 13.2 the business layer is accountable for appointing the executive and the project manager; the executive is responsible (13.6).

whyNot.0: The executive is responsible for this activity, not accountable.
whyNot.1: The project manager is being appointed; the role does not own the appointment.
whyNot.3: Project assurance is not involved in this activity.

A.q: During starting up at Fernhollow Foods, the project manager must define what the project will deliver (six chilled meals, an eight-day shelf life and kerbside-recyclable packs) and create the project product description. Which roles should she consult?
options: The business layer, the executive and project assurance
The executive, the senior user and the senior supplier
The senior user, the team managers and project support
The senior supplier, project assurance and project support
A.why: In prepare the outline business case the PM consults the senior user, senior supplier and executive to define what the project will deliver and create the PPD (13.4.3).

whyNot.0: The business layer provides the mandate; the recommended consultation is with the three board roles.
whyNot.2: Team managers and support are not the roles named for defining the project product.
whyNot.3: This leaves out the executive and senior user, whose views define what is needed.

B.q: Fernhollow's executive, Imogen Fairley, is choosing a senior user and a senior supplier for the Fernhollow Kitchen board, so that business, user and supplier interests are all represented. Which role should be responsible for the 'appoint the project management team' activity?
options: The business layer
The project manager
The senior user
The executive
B.why: Tab 13.2 makes the executive responsible for appointing the project management team, with the business layer accountable (13.4.4, 13.6).

whyNot.0: The business layer is accountable for the appointments; the executive carries them out.
whyNot.1: The project manager is not involved in appointing the project management team.
whyNot.2: The senior user is one of the roles being appointed, not the appointer.

B.q: Fernhollow's project manager has the outline business case, the project product description, the hybrid project approach and the team's role descriptions. She now draws them together into one document that will give a firm basis for initiation. Which activity is this, and what does it produce?
options: Assemble the project brief, producing the project brief
Request project initiation, producing a request to initiate
Plan the initiation stage, producing the initiation stage plan
Prepare the outline business case, producing the PPD
B.why: Assemble the project brief brings the earlier starting up outputs together into the project brief, the foundation for initiation (ch 13).

whyNot.1: The request asks the board for authority; it is not where the outputs are combined into one document.
whyNot.2: The initiation stage plan schedules the initiation work; it does not combine these products.
whyNot.3: The PPD and outline business case already exist; combining them with the others is the brief.

B.q: Fernhollow's initiation will take four weeks. Before asking for authority, the project manager lists the initiation work (agreeing the management approaches, preparing the project plan), who will do it and when, so the board can approve the time and people. Which activity is this, and why?
options: Establish project controls, so the board can control the initiation work
Prepare the project plan, so the launch date can be checked early
Plan the initiation stage, so that initiation is not aimless
Request project initiation, so the board can release the funding
B.why: Initiation takes time and resources, so it is planned and approved in plan the initiation stage to stop it being aimless and unstructured (13.4.7).

whyNot.0: Establish project controls is an initiating a project activity that sets control for after initiation.
whyNot.1: The project plan is prepared later, inside initiating a project.
whyNot.3: The request comes after the plan exists and presents it; listing the initiation work is the planning activity.

C.q: At the end of starting up, Fernhollow's project manager gives the directors a short verbal pitch on why the range is worth initiating and asks to begin initiation the next day. She has not yet planned the initiation stage. Is this an appropriate application of the 'request project initiation' activity, and why?
options: Yes, because the PM usually explains the case to the board verbally
Yes, because authority to initiate can be given without a formal meeting
No, because starting up is incomplete without an initiation stage plan
No, because the request for initiation should come from the executive
C.why: The request presents the approach, the appointments and the initiation stage activities and controls; starting up is not complete until the initiation stage plan exists (13.4.8).

whyNot.0: It is true the PM often explains the options verbally, but that does not make a request without an initiation plan complete.
whyNot.1: The board can authorize without a meeting, but that does not explain whether the request itself was complete.
whyNot.3: The project manager makes the request to the board; that is not the problem here.

C.q: Fernhollow's executive, Imogen Fairley, is busy with a supermarket audit. She asks the project manager, Nadia Osei, to choose and appoint the senior supplier because Nadia has met the design agency. Is this an appropriate application of the 'appoint the project management team' activity, and why?
options: Yes, because the PM manages the project day to day for the executive
Yes, because the team must reflect business, user and supplier interests
No, because the business layer should make each appointment itself
No, because the executive is responsible for appointing the team
C.why: Tab 13.2 makes the executive responsible and the business layer accountable for appointing the PMT; the PM is not involved (13.4.4, 13.6).

whyNot.0: The PM does run the project day to day, but that does not extend to appointing the board.
whyNot.1: Balanced interests are an aim of the activity, but they do not make the PM the right person to appoint.
whyNot.2: The business layer is accountable; the executive, not the business layer, carries out the appointments.

C.q: During starting up, Fernhollow's project manager runs a workshop with the executive, the senior user and the senior supplier to agree what the range must deliver: six meals, an eight-day shelf life and kerbside-recyclable packs. She records this in the project product description and keeps the outline business case high-level. Is this an appropriate application of the 'prepare the outline business case' activity, and why?
options: Yes, because the senior user is accountable for specifying benefits
Yes, because the PM consults these roles to define the project product
No, because the project product description is created in initiation
No, because the outline business case should show detailed costs
C.why: In prepare the outline business case the PM consults the senior user, senior supplier and executive to define what the project will deliver and creates the PPD; the outline case is a high-level view at this point (13.4.3).

whyNot.0: It is true the senior user specifies benefits, but that does not explain this workshop about the project product.
whyNot.2: The PPD is created in starting up, alongside the outline business case.
whyNot.3: Detailed costs come from the project plan in initiation; the outline case is high-level.

reteach.title: Who does what before initiation
reteach.question: Can you match each starting up activity to the role that owns or carries out the key step?

blocks.h: Three roles do most of the work
blocks.body: The business layer issues the mandate and owns the appointments. The executive makes the appointments. The project manager does almost everything else: lessons, the outline business case and PPD (after consulting the board roles), the approach, the brief, the initiation stage plan and the request.

head: Activity
Key role
rows: PM asks; board decides in DP

blocks.text: If an option has the project manager appointing board members, it is wrong: the PM is not involved in appointing the project management team.

explain.body: The business layer is accountable for both appointment activities and the executive is responsible. The PM, once appointed, runs the project day to day on the executive's behalf, but takes no part in appointing the rest of the team.

test.q: Fernhollow's executive has appointed a senior user and a senior supplier for the Fernhollow Kitchen board. Which role should be accountable for these appointments?
options: The executive
The business layer
The project manager
Project support
test.why: The business layer is accountable for 'appoint the project management team'; the executive is responsible (13.6, tab 13.2).

whyNot.0: The executive is responsible: it carries out the appointments.
whyNot.2: The project manager is not involved in appointing the project management team.
whyNot.3: Project support is not involved in this activity.

explain.body: Assess previous lessons consults people and teams with experience of similar projects and creates the lessons log. Prepare the outline business case is high-level; the PM consults the executive, senior user and senior supplier to define what will be delivered and creates the PPD.

test.q: Fernhollow's project manager is drafting the outline business case. The finance director asks her to include a detailed investment appraisal using line-by-line costs for every stage, although no project plan exists yet. What should the outline business case contain at this point?
options: A high-level view that initiation will develop
Detailed stage costs taken from supplier quotes
The approved figures from the project plan
Benefits measured against the launch results
test.why: With little information yet available, the outline business case stays high-level; initiating a project later builds the detailed business case on it (13.4.3).

whyNot.1: Detailed costs come later, when the project plan is prepared in initiation.
whyNot.2: The project plan does not exist yet; it is prepared in initiating a project.
whyNot.3: Benefits are measured after delivery; the outline case forecasts them.

explain.body: Select the project approach decides how the work will be done: in-house or by third parties, build or buy, and the delivery method. Assemble the project brief brings the outline business case, PPD, approach and team structure together into the brief.

root.label: How will the work be done?

test.q: Fernhollow's project manager and the board roles decide that two recipes needing a pan-frying process will be made by a co-manufacturer rather than by buying new equipment. In which starting up activity should this be decided?
options: Prepare the outline business case
Appoint the project management team
Assemble the project brief
Select the project approach
test.why: Select the project approach answers how the work will be approached, for example in-house or by third parties, build or buy (13.4.5).

whyNot.0: The outline business case justifies the project; the build-or-buy choice is part of the approach.
whyNot.1: Appointing the team decides who sits in the PMT roles, not how the work is sourced.
whyNot.2: The brief records the approach once it has been selected.

explain.body: Plan the initiation stage produces the initiation stage plan so initiation is not aimless. Request project initiation then formally asks the board for authority to initiate, presenting the approach, the team appointments and the initiation stage activities and controls.

test.q: Fernhollow's project manager is preparing the request for project initiation. Which content should the request present to the board?
options: The PID, the project plan and the full business case
The approved stage plan for the concept stage
The approach, team appointments and initiation plans
The lessons report and the end stage report
test.why: The request presents the project approach, the project management team appointments and the initiation stage activities and controls (13.4.8).

whyNot.0: The PID, project plan and full business case are produced in initiating a project.
whyNot.1: The concept stage plan is prepared in managing a stage boundary at the end of initiation.
whyNot.3: These reports belong to later stage ends and closure.
